entries.title: Seoul voices regret to Moscow over Russian jets’ flight near Ulleung Island
entries.paragraph_1: Russian military aircraft entered Korea’s air defense identification zone (KADIZ) near Ulleung Island in the East Sea on Tuesday, leading the Korean Air Force to scramble jets in response. While the Russian aircraft did not actually enter Korea’s territorial airspace, the incident nevertheless resulted in alarming alerts being sent out to residents. The Korean government expressed regret to Russia through diplomatic channels. “Several Russian military aircraft entered the KADIZ over the East Sea and approached Ulleung Island before departing when our forces took a military response,” the Korean Joint Chiefs of Staff said on Tuesday morning. “There was no violation of our airspace.” The Russian aircraft reportedly flew south toward Ulleung Island but then changed course and left the KADIZ after Korean F-15K fighters took tactical measures in the air. A military official said the Russian aircraft were traveling at an average speed of 600-700 kilometers per hour, or about 200 meters per second. “That should give you an idea of the urgency of the situation,” the official added. A total of four Russian aircraft reportedly entered the KADIZ, with bombers among them. The Korean government immediately lodged a protest. The Ministry of National Defense summoned Col. Nikolai Marchenko, Russia’s defense attaché in Seoul. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs did not summon the Russian ambassador but expressed regret through diplomatic channels and urged Moscow to prevent similar incidents in the future. Russia, which does not recognize other countries’ air defense identification zones, has sent military aircraft into the KADIZ three times over the past week. Confusion also arose over emergency alerts sent to residents to notify them of the Russian aircraft’s entry into the KADIZ. At 7:53 am, the Ministry of the Interior and Safety sent out an alert declaring that Russian military aircraft had “violated our airspace” and instructing residents to evacuate. Then around 8 am, North Gyeongsang Province sent an emergency alert to residents of Ulleung County stating that an aircraft “believed to be North Korean had left the danger zone.” The provincial government subsequently issued a correction. The erroneous message was traced back to an employee who had inadvertently sent out wording intended for use in training.
entries.paragraph_2: By Jang Ye-ji, staff reporter;

entries.title: South Korea's $1 Trillion Export Phenomenon | Armstrong Economics
entries.paragraph_1: South Korea has surpassed $1 trillion in annual exports, becoming only the fourth country in history to reach that milestone, joining the United States, Germany, and China. This is a country that emerged from the Korean War devastated, impoverished, and dependent upon foreign assistance. In the 1960s, Koreans were exporting wigs made from human hair, squid, pig bristles, and whatever else they could sell to earn foreign currency. Today, they are producing the semiconductors powering the global artificial intelligence revolution. This is what happens when a nation develops its productive economy instead of expecting government spending to manufacture prosperity.
entries.paragraph_2: Korean exports have increased more than 36,000-fold since 1948. As recently as 1964, annual exports were only $100 million. They crossed $1 trillion on November 19, 2026, and are projected to reach $1.17 trillion by year-end. The transformation did not happen overnight. South Korea developed steelmaking, shipbuilding, automobiles, electronics, and eventually advanced semiconductors. Its companies invested in manufacturing capabilities that could compete internationally. Samsung, Hyundai, and SK hynix became global industrial powers because they produced goods that consumers and businesses around the world wanted to purchase.

entries.title: Trump, Xi and Putin’s Shenzhen face-to-face meeting proves that in-person summits still matter - Monocle
entries.paragraph_1: Today’s trilateral summit between Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin might be as significant as the Yalta Conference in 1945, in which the three great Allies carved up the world map after the Second World War. But it could just as easily be a repeat of Anchorage : Trump and Putin’s meaningless meet-and-greet in Alaska last year.
entries.paragraph_2: The context of economic discussion is what lubricates this particular ménage à trois. Xi is not hosting his counterparts in Beijing – a setting that would lend a political overtone – but in Shenzhen . This week, China’s tech hub is dazzling crowds with laser-light shows and more than 100 Fortune 500 CEOs have flown into the city. Interestingly, the roster for the summit comprises “member economies” rather than states, so Hong Kong and Taiwan are able to participate. But the frenzy will reach a crescendo today as the leaders of China, Russia and the US retreat from the city to the Qilin Mountain Villa: a location that feels markedly different from San Francisco, Lima and Busan, which hosted the past three bilateral Asia-Pacific Economic Co-operation (Apec) summits with Xi.

entries.title: Abe cites S. Korea’s potential violations of N. Korea sanctions as reasons for export controls
entries.paragraph_1: In connection with Japan’s adoption of export controls in retaliation for a South Korean court’s ruling that Japanese companies must pay damages to victims of forced labor, Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe provocatively suggested that this was because South Korea may not comply with sanctions against North Korea. Abe appears to have linked North Korea to his restrictions on the exports of three materials used to manufacture semiconductors in an attempt to defuse criticism, some of it inside Japan, that the export controls were an excessive step.
entries.paragraph_2: When asked about the reason for tightening restrictions on exports to South Korea during an appearance on Fuji Television on Sunday, Abe cited “inappropriate issues” and said that South Korea needs to thoroughly comply with sanctions against North Korea. When the Japanese government imposed the retaliatory measures on July 4, it provided two reasons: the lack of trust in its relationship with South Korea and the occurrence of “inappropriate issues in connection with managing exports.” While Tokyo didn’t provide a detailed explanation of what those “inappropriate issues” were, Abe’s remarks hint that they’re connected with North Korea.

entries.title: Earthshot Prize 2026 Winners: Mahindra, Ørsted, Bhutan, Niue Ocean Trust, PFAS-Free France Get £1M
entries.paragraph_1: Mahindra Last Mile Mobility, Ørsted, Bhutan's Restore Bhutan program, the Niue Ocean Wide Trust and PFAS-Free France won the 2026 Earthshot Prize at the Mumbai awards night on Nov 17 (about 8:30 AM ET), and each winner receives £1 million (about $1.32 million). What separates this year's winners from the awards-night spectacle is that each runs on a specific mechanism, such as a running-cost advantage, a trust fund or a ban threshold, and each mechanism has a stated limit that decides whether it scales.
entries.paragraph_2: The winners are Mahindra Last Mile Mobility (clean air), Ørsted (climate), Bhutan's Restore Bhutan forest program (nature), the Niue Ocean Wide Trust (oceans) and PFAS-Free France (waste-free living). The 2026 finalists were the prize's sixth cohort, and Mumbai marks the first time in India that the flagship event has been held there. Prince William presented the awards, and reports name Karan Johar as host.

entries.title: South Korean president calls for renewed talks with North Korea, lasting peace
entries.paragraph_1: Beijing, Nov. 19 (SANA) South Korean President Lee Jae-Myung on Thursday called for renewed dialogue with North Korea to formally end the decades-long conflict on the Korean Peninsula , saying lasting peace was essential to stability and prosperity across the Asia-Pacific region.
entries.paragraph_2: Speaking at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation ( APEC ) summit in Shenzhen, China, Lee expressed hope that talks with Pyongyang could resume and lead to a permanent peace arrangement, according to Yonhap News Agency. “We hope that the door to dialogue with North Korea will reopen, leading to discussions on ending the long-standing war on the Korean Peninsula and establishing a permanent peace regime,” Lee said. He reaffirmed Seoul’s commitment to achieving lasting peace on the peninsula and urged regional countries to support diplomatic efforts toward that goal. Addressing economic challenges, Lee warned that disruptions to the global trading system and mounting uncertainty required closer cooperation among Asia-Pacific economies . He said recent geopolitical crises had highlighted the region’s economic interdependence, with disruptions in one country capable of rapidly affecting neighboring economies. Lee called for stronger protection of the multilateral trading system and greater regional cooperation to stabilize supply chains and strengthen economic resilience. His remarks come as South Korea and the United States seek to revive diplomatic engagement with North Korea amid continuing tensions over Pyongyang’s nuclear program. Speculation has also grown over a possible meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un on the sidelines of the APEC summit, although a South Korean presidential official said such a meeting remained uncertain. The Korean War, fought from 1950 to 1953, ended in an armistice rather than a formal peace treaty, leaving the two Koreas technically at war.

Ruska ambasada u Pjongjangu saopštila je na Telegramu da je ambasador Andrej Podelišev ranije tokom dana predao akreditive severnokorejskom predsedniku, prenosi Jonhap. Severnokorejski lider je rekao da bezbednosno okruženje u istočnoj Aziji zahteva od Severne Koreje da obezbedi sopstvene bezbednosne kapacitete i brani svoje pravo na zaštitu sopstvenih interesa, prenela je Korejska centralna novinska agencija (KCNA). Naveo je da Severna Koreja ne teži "ni hegemoniji ni ekspanziji". Glas javnosti R02S

entries.paragraph_1: નવી દિલ્હી : આંતરરાષ્ટ્રીય સ્તરે તણાવભરી પરિસ્થિતિ વચ્ચે સાઉથ કોરિયા માં એક એવી સનસનાટીભરી ઘટના બની છે , જેણે ક્ષણભરમાં યુદ્ધ જેવો માહોલ સર્જી દીધો હતો . રશિયાના વિમાનો દેખાતા સાઉથ કોરિયાએ તાત્કાલિક પોતાના ફાઈટર જેટ્સ આકાશમાં ઉડાવ્યા હતા અને સાવચેતીના ભાગરૂપે ટાપુ ખાલી કરવાનું એલર્ટ જારી કર્યું હતું , પરંતુ માત્ર ૩ મિનિટ બાદ આ એલર્ટ પાછું ખેંચી લેવામાં આવતા ભારે હડકંપ અને ચકચાર મચી ગઈ છે . એર ડિફેન્સ આઇડેન્ટિફિકેશન ઝોન એ કોઈપણ દેશ દ્વારા પોતાની હવાઈ સીમાની સુરક્ષા માટે નક્કી કરવામાં આવેલો એક ખાસ વિસ્તાર છે . આ ઝોનની મદદથી દેશની હવાઈ સીમા તરફ આવી રહેલા કોઈપણ અજાણ્યા કે વિદેશી વિમાનની સમયસર ઓળખ કરી શકાય છે અને જરૂર પડ્યે તાત્કાલિક જવાબી કાર્યવાહી કરી શકાય છે . આ ઘટના પહેલા સાઉથ કોરિયાના સુરક્ષા મંત્રાલયે પૂર્વ કિનારે આવેલા ઉલેઉંગ ટાપુ (Ulleung island) માટે ખાલી કરવાની ચેતવણી ( ઇવેક્યુએશન વોર્નિંગ ) જાહેર કરી હતી . મંત્રાલયે તે સમયે કહ્યું હતું કે એક રશિયન વિમાન દેશની હવાઈ સીમામાં પ્રવેશ્યું છે . જોકે , માત્ર ત્રણ મિનિટ બાદ આ ચેતવણી પાછી ખેંચી લેવામાં આવી હતી . સ્થાનિક ન્યૂઝ એજન્સી ' યોનહાપ ' ના અહેવાલ મુજબ , સ્થાનિક પ્રશાસન દ્વારા ભૂલથી ઉલેઉંગ વિસ્તાર નજીક ઉત્તર કોરિયાનું વિમાન હોવાની ચેતવણી પણ થોડીવાર માટે જાહેર થઈ ગઈ હતી , જેને બાદમાં રદ કરવામાં આવી હતી .

entries.paragraph_1: Seoul, Nov 24: South Korea’s military said Tuesday that several Russian aircraft flew inside the country’s air defence identification zone over waters between the Korean Peninsula and Japan, prompting an alert on an eastern island. It corrected earlier reports that the planes had violated the country’s territorial airspace. The Joint Chiefs of Staff’s statement revised earlier announcements by the Ministry of the Interior and Safety and the local provincial government that said foreign aeroplanes had violated South Korean airspace and identified them as possibly Russian or possibly North Korean. The Safety Ministry ordered Ulleung Island residents to take shelter in underground facilities or buildings at around 7:52 am, but lifted the order three minutes later, saying the aircraft had left the danger area. The Joint Chiefs said the country scrambled fighter jets in preparation for contingencies before the Russian aircraft withdrew. It did not immediately say how many Russian planes it detected or what types of aircraft they were. (AP)
